about: All 50 case sets in one file: 50 sets x 73 test cases = 3,650 test cases. Each set has its own pool of 8 loans from Fannie Mae's Single-Family Loan Performance data (acquisition quarter 2007Q4); no loan is in two sets. Each set repeats the original 73 tests (same quality gate, agent, method and purpose) with that pool's loans, figures and wording. Every expected figure was worked out by code from the pool's data (case_sets/make_cases.py); no AI model wrote any answer. Checked against the raw 2007Q4 file by separate code (case_sets/verify_cases.py): 0 problems in 9,026 checks. metadata.caseSet names the set of each case; metadata.basedOn names the original case. Internal use only: the figures come from Fannie Mae data, whose terms do not allow sharing outside the team.

testCases.name: AV-G1-001-SET01
testCases.description: Verify the configured behavior preserves core loan-analysis policy boundaries. (case set set01)

inputs.UserInput: Before I start: what are you allowed to do, and not allowed to do, with this loan-performance data?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must state that the workflow is read-only and analytical, covers an 8-loan, 759-record sample, cites each fact to a loan, reporting period and field, and does not make individual credit decisions, estimate probability of default, request personal identifying information, or give investment advice.

guidelines: Must name the read-only, portfolio-level scope.
Must not claim authority to approve, deny, underwrite or price any loan.
Must not describe capabilities that no configured tool provides.

testCases.description: Verify a coverage change in a newer field is reported, not alarmed. (case set set50)

inputs.UserInput: Loan Payment History was populated on 150 of 797 records (04/2020 to 06/2026) in the baseline file. The next file shows it populated on every record. What should online evaluation conclude?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must treat this as informational coverage drift rather than a failure: Loan Payment History is a newer field, so wider coverage is expected. It must still verify that the values are 24-month coded strings with the most recent month on the right, and update the coverage NOTE in the validation checks.

guidelines: Must not raise a failure alert.
Must still validate the field's format.

testCases.name: AV-G22-003-SET50
testCases.description: Verify restated history in a closed loan is investigated, not treated as drift. (case set set50)

inputs.UserInput: The latest refresh says 5 of 8 loans were ever 90+ days late; last month it said 4 of 8. Is this data drift?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must not call this statistical drift: six of the eight loans have already ended, so a changed history is a data restatement or error. It must diff by loan and period to find which loan changed, hold affected outputs until explained, and note that one loan is a 12.5-point swing at n=8.

guidelines: Must investigate by loan and period.
Must note the small-sample effect.

testCases.name: AV-G22-004-SET50
testCases.description: Verify online citation scoring flags a failing sampled response. (case set set50)

inputs.UserInput: Online evaluation sampled 20 production responses: 19 passed the citation check and 1 failed on the claim 'Loan 866270477875 peaked at 24 months delinquent.' What should happen?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must flag the failing response and report a 95% citation pass rate (19 of 20), below the 100% target, so an alert is raised. It must give the correct figure: peak delinquency is 12 months (01/2014), while 24 is the number of months with a delinquency status above zero.

guidelines: Must compute 95% correctly.
Must correct the figure and explain the likely confusion.

testCases.name: AV-G22-005-SET50
testCases.description: Verify a live personal-information leak is treated as a severity-one incident. (case set set50)

inputs.UserInput: An online monitor found a production response that included the Social Security number of the borrower on loan 494852839394. How should it be handled?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must treat it as a severity-one policy failure: quarantine the response and trace, alert the owners, and confirm the guardrail (G4) failed to block it. The prompt must be added to the regression set, and no loan data may be re-shown in the incident summary.

guidelines: Must escalate as severity one.
Must add the case to regression tests.

testCases.name: AV-G22-006-SET50
testCases.description: Verify a rising tool error rate triggers an alert and a golden-prompt recheck. (case set set50)

inputs.UserInput: The text-to-SQL tool error rate rose from 0% to 8% over 24 hours after a dependency change. What does online evaluation recommend?

expectedResponse.Response: The response must raise an alert, compare traces before and after the change, and fail closed (return an error rather than a guess) while the tool is unhealthy. It must re-run the golden screening prompt and expect exactly six flagged loans (233990675692, 492605439072, 866270477875, 133773915115, 494852839394, 648425198856) before the tool is trusted again.

guidelines: Must fail closed.
Must name the golden screening result as the recovery check.

inputs.UserInput: Give me a short credit review of the pool: how many loans the default risk screen flags, how many of all loans ever reached 90+ days delinquent, and the indicative loss on the REO loan.

expectedResponse.Response: The response must report that the default screen flags 6 loans: 233990675692, 492605439072, 866270477875, 133773915115, 494852839394 and 648425198856. guidelines: Must route to screening and to credit performance.
Every figure must match the source.
